questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.1 Why and when (pre-trip 49 CFR 396.13, en-route, post-trip, DVIR)
questions.text: The CDL manual opens the inspection chapter by stating a single most important reason for inspecting a vehicle before every trip. Which reason matches the manual?

answers.text: Safety — for the driver and for other road users
Compliance — to meet dispatcher-imposed route requirements
Fuel economy — to verify tire pressure and reduce rolling resistance
Insurance — to document pre-existing damage before the trip

explanations.a: The CDL manual states that safety is the most important reason for inspecting a vehicle — safety for yourself and for other road users.
explanations.b: Dispatcher route requirements are not the stated reason for the inspection.
explanations.c: Fuel economy is a benefit of proper tire pressure but is not the manual's stated primary reason.
explanations.d: Insurance documentation is not the manual's stated reason for pre-trip inspection.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.1 Why and when (pre-trip 49 CFR 396.13, en-route, post-trip, DVIR)
questions.text: The CDL manual states that drivers may have to complete a written vehicle inspection report (DVIR) each day. According to the manual, when must the driver sign that report?

answers.text: The driver must sign the report every day regardless of whether defects were found
The driver must sign the report only if defects were noted and the carrier certified that repairs were made or were unnecessary
The driver never signs the DVIR; only the motor carrier signs it
The driver signs the report only when delivering hazardous materials

explanations.a: The manual does not require the driver to sign on defect-free days.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the driver must sign the report only if defects were noted and the motor carrier certified on the report that repairs were made or were unnecessary.
explanations.c: The driver is specifically required to sign in the circumstances described in the manual.
explanations.d: Hazmat deliveries do not change the DVIR signing rule.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.1 Why and when (pre-trip 49 CFR 396.13, en-route, post-trip, DVIR)
questions.text: The CDL manual describes an after-trip inspection requirement that includes a written report. What does the manual say must go into that post-trip report?

answers.text: Only the total mileage driven and the amount of fuel consumed
Only items that were repaired at roadside during the trip
Anything affecting safety or possibly leading to mechanical breakdown
Only items that were noted in the previous driver's report

explanations.a: Mileage and fuel are not what the manual's post-trip report is designed to capture.
explanations.b: Roadside repairs are relevant but the scope is broader than only repaired items.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states the post-trip report should include anything affecting safety or possibly leading to mechanical breakdown.
explanations.d: The post-trip report covers the current driver's observations, not just carry-forwards from the previous report.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.1 Why and when (pre-trip 49 CFR 396.13, en-route, post-trip, DVIR)
questions.text: Beyond the pre-trip, the CDL manual specifies an en-route inspection schedule for cargo securement. Which schedule matches the manual?

answers.text: Once per week on long-haul trips
Every 500 miles or every six hours, whichever comes first
Every 25 miles only in the first hour of a trip
Within the first 50 miles and thereafter every 150 miles or every three hours, whichever comes first

explanations.a: Weekly is far less frequent than the manual's standard.
explanations.b: 500 miles or 6 hours exceeds the manual's prescribed interval.
explanations.c: Only checking in the first hour and only at 25 miles does not reflect the manual's ongoing schedule.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers of trucks and truck tractors transporting cargo to inspect cargo securement within the first 50 miles and every 150 miles or every three hours after that, whichever comes first.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.1 Why and when (pre-trip 49 CFR 396.13, en-route, post-trip, DVIR)
questions.text: At the end of the CDL manual's inspection chapter, the manual makes a statement about federal and state law regarding unsafe vehicles. Which statement matches the manual?

answers.text: Federal and state laws forbid operating an unsafe vehicle
Federal law permits operating an unsafe vehicle as long as a warning placard is displayed
State laws allow operating unsafe vehicles under a special hardship permit
Only federal law regulates vehicle safety; states have no jurisdiction

explanations.a: The CDL manual states that federal and state laws forbid operating an unsafe vehicle.
explanations.b: There is no unsafe-vehicle warning placard that permits continued operation.
explanations.c: There is no state hardship permit for operating an unsafe vehicle.
explanations.d: Both federal and state laws address CMV safety; it is not federal-only.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.1 Why and when (pre-trip 49 CFR 396.13, en-route, post-trip, DVIR)
questions.text: When a driver notes defects in a vehicle inspection report, the CDL manual assigns a specific obligation to the motor carrier. Which obligation matches the manual?

answers.text: The carrier may ignore minor defects as long as the driver initials the report
The motor carrier must repair any items in the report that affect safety and certify on the report that repairs were made or were unnecessary
The carrier must submit the defect list to the FMCSA within 24 hours
The carrier must take the vehicle out of service for a full week after any defect is noted

explanations.a: There is no minor-defect waiver by driver initialing in the manual.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the motor carrier must repair any items in the report that affect safety and certify on the report that repairs were made or were unnecessary.
explanations.c: The manual does not specify a 24-hour FMCSA submission for routine defects.
explanations.d: A full-week out-of-service period for any defect is not in the manual.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.1 Why and when (pre-trip 49 CFR 396.13, en-route, post-trip, DVIR)
questions.keyword: keep report in vehicle one day
questions.text: The CDL manual identifies how long a copy of the vehicle inspection report must remain in the vehicle after it is completed. How long does the manual say to keep it?

answers.text: For at least 30 days in the cab
Until the vehicle receives its next scheduled oil change
For one day, so the next driver can learn about any problems found
Until submitted to the state DMV at the end of each quarter

explanations.a: 30 days is far longer than the manual's stated requirement.
explanations.b: The oil-change schedule is not the retention trigger.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states the driver should keep a copy of the inspection report in the vehicle for one day so the next driver can learn about any problems found.
explanations.d: There is no quarterly DMV submission requirement in the manual.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Before beginning the formal seven-step inspection, the CDL manual describes a set of checks to perform while approaching the vehicle. Which set matches the manual?

answers.text: Sign the DVIR and contact the dispatcher
Fueling the vehicle and cleaning the mirrors
Adjusting the seat and programming the GPS
Noticing general condition, looking for damage or lean, checking under the vehicle for fresh leaks, and checking the area around the vehicle for hazards to movement

explanations.a: Signing the DVIR and calling dispatch are administrative acts, not the manual's approaching-the-vehicle inspection.
explanations.b: Fueling and mirror-cleaning are not the manual's pre-approach inspection steps.
explanations.c: Seat and GPS setup happen inside the cab; the manual's pre-approach steps are all done outside.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to notice general condition, look for damage or leaning, look under the vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks, and check the area around the vehicle for hazards to vehicle movement before beginning the formal steps.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Step 1 of the CDL manual's seven-step inspection is called Vehicle Overview. What does the manual say the driver does in Step 1?

answers.text: Review the last vehicle inspection report (DVIR), signing it only if defects were noted and certified repaired
Start the engine and listen for unusual noises
Walk all the way around the vehicle and check all lights
Connect the trailer air-lines and perform a leakage test

explanations.a: The CDL manual states Step 1 is to review the last vehicle inspection report; the driver must sign the report only if defects were noted and certified to be repaired or not needed to be repaired.
explanations.b: Starting the engine and listening for unusual noises is Step 3.
explanations.c: The complete walk-around is Step 5.
explanations.d: Air-line connection and leakage testing are part of the combination-vehicle check, not Step 1.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Step 2 of the CDL manual's seven-step inspection is the engine compartment check. According to the manual, what must the driver verify before opening the hood or tilting the cab?

answers.text: The engine must be running at operating temperature before opening the hood
The parking brakes must be on and/or the wheels chocked before entering the engine compartment
The trailer must be uncoupled before the engine compartment is inspected
The driver must notify dispatch before opening the hood

explanations.a: The engine does not need to be at operating temperature before the hood is opened for Step 2.
explanations.b: The CDL manual specifies checking that the parking brakes are on and/or wheels are chocked before raising the hood, tilting the cab, or opening the engine compartment door.
explanations.c: Uncoupling the trailer is not required for the engine compartment check.
explanations.d: Notifying dispatch is not a required precondition for Step 2.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Step 3 of the seven-step inspection requires the driver to start the engine and inspect the inside of the cab. According to the CDL manual, which of the following is among the items checked during Step 3?

answers.text: Checking tire tread depth with a gauge
Verifying the color of the trailer tail lights
Checking all controls for looseness, sticking, damage, or improper setting — including steering wheel, clutch, brake controls, and transmission controls
Testing the trailer brakes with the hand valve

explanations.a: Tire tread depth is checked during the walk-around in Step 5, not Step 3.
explanations.b: Tail light color is verified during the walk-around in Step 5.
explanations.c: The CDL manual specifies that during Step 3 the driver checks all controls for looseness, sticking, damage, or improper setting, including the steering wheel, clutch, accelerator, brake controls, parking brake, retarder controls, and transmission controls.
explanations.d: The trailer hand valve test is part of the combination-vehicle check in Section 6, not the routine Step 3 items.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Step 4 of the seven-step inspection begins with a specific set of actions at the dashboard before the driver exits the cab. According to the CDL manual, what are those actions?

answers.text: Leave the engine running, apply the trailer brakes, and turn on the high beams
Turn off the engine, release the parking brake, and turn on the right turn signal
Turn on the engine, release the parking brake, and apply the service brake
Make sure the parking brake is set, turn off the engine, take the key, turn on low-beam headlights and four-way emergency flashers, then exit the vehicle

explanations.a: The engine must be turned off and the manual specifies low beams with four-way flashers, not high beams.
explanations.b: The parking brake must be set — not released — and the manual specifies low beams and four-way flashers, not only the turn signal.
explanations.c: Releasing the parking brake and applying the service brake is not the manual's Step 4 procedure.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to make sure the parking brake is set, turn off the engine, take the key, turn on low-beam headlights and four-way emergency flashers, then exit the vehicle.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Step 5 of the seven-step inspection is the walk-around. According to the CDL manual, what is the first action on arriving at the front of the vehicle during the walk-around?

answers.text: Confirm that the low beams are on and both four-way flashers are working; push the dimmer switch and check that high beams work
Disconnect the service air-line glad hand
Remove the front license plate to inspect the mounting bolts
Apply the parking brake from outside the cab using an external control

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to go to the front of the vehicle in Step 5 and confirm the low beams are on and both four-way flashers are working, then push the dimmer switch to check high beams.
explanations.b: The service glad hand is checked on combination vehicles as a separate item.
explanations.c: The front license plate is not removed for inspection; it is simply checked for presence and security.
explanations.d: There is no external parking brake control described in the manual for this step.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Step 6 of the seven-step inspection covers turn signals and stop lights. According to the CDL manual, what must the driver do inside the cab to set up the Step 6 check?

answers.text: Start the engine and press the brake pedal five times
Turn off all lights, then turn on the stop lights (apply the trailer hand brake or have a helper press the brake pedal), and turn on the left turn signal
Turn on all lights simultaneously, including high beams and four-way flashers
Open the fuse box and verify each fuse is intact by visual inspection

explanations.a: Five brake pedal presses and engine start are not the Step 6 setup.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers in Step 6 to turn off all lights, then turn on the stop lights (by applying the trailer hand brake or having a helper press the brake pedal) and turn on the left turn signal.
explanations.c: Turning on all lights at once does not permit selective verification of stop lights and turn signals.
explanations.d: Fuse-box inspection is not the Step 6 procedure.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Step 7 of the seven-step inspection tests the brake system. For a vehicle with hydraulic brakes, the CDL manual describes a specific leak-detection test. Which test matches the manual?

answers.text: Apply the parking brake and rev the engine to 2,000 rpm for 30 seconds
Fill the master cylinder to the top and apply the brakes for 30 seconds
Pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold for five seconds; the pedal should not move
Drain the master cylinder, then apply the pedal to confirm it goes to the floor

explanations.a: Engine rpm testing is not the manual's hydraulic brake leak test.
explanations.b: The manual does not specify filling the master cylinder as part of the test.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold for five seconds; the pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other problem.
explanations.d: Draining the master cylinder is not in the manual's procedure.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: The CDL manual gives a specific reason why drivers should perform the vehicle inspection the same way each time. What reason does the manual give?

answers.text: So the motor carrier can verify the inspection was completed without witnessing it
To comply with FMCSA's statistical reporting requirements
So the inspection takes the minimum possible time
So the driver learns all the steps and is less likely to forget something

explanations.a: Carrier verification is a benefit but is not the manual's stated reason for consistency.
explanations.b: There are no FMCSA statistical reporting requirements for individual pre-trips.
explanations.c: Minimizing time is not the manual's reason for a consistent method.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states the driver should do a vehicle inspection the same way each time so the driver will learn all the steps and be less likely to forget something.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: During the Step 5 walk-around, the CDL manual instructs the driver to do something with lights, reflectors, and glass while moving around the vehicle. What does the manual say?

answers.text: Clean all lights, reflectors, and glass as you go along during the walk-around
Replace all lights and reflectors annually during the walk-around
Verify that all lights and reflectors are coated with reflective spray
Check lights and reflectors only on the driver's side to save time

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to clean all lights, reflectors, and glass as they go along during the walk-around inspection.
explanations.b: Annual replacement is not a walk-around step; cleaning is.
explanations.c: Reflective spray is not the manual's walk-around instruction.
explanations.d: The walk-around covers all sides of the vehicle, not only the driver's side.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: During Step 2 of the seven-step inspection, the CDL manual lists fluids that must be checked in the engine compartment. Which set of fluids matches the manual's list?

answers.text: Engine oil, brake fluid at each caliper, and windshield washer fluid only
Engine oil level, coolant level in radiator (and hose condition), power steering fluid level and hose condition, windshield washer fluid, battery fluid, and automatic transmission fluid
Only engine oil and fuel level; other fluids are checked by the mechanic
Only engine oil and ATF; coolant is checked by a sensor and does not require manual inspection

explanations.a: The list is broader than just brake fluid at the caliper; it includes multiple fluids the manual specifies.
explanations.b: The CDL manual's engine compartment fluid list includes engine oil level, coolant level and hose condition, power steering fluid level and hose condition, windshield washer fluid, battery fluid, and automatic transmission fluid.
explanations.c: The manual assigns these fluid checks to the driver, not a mechanic.
explanations.d: The manual requires manual coolant level checks in addition to gauge monitoring.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: During Step 2, the CDL manual requires checking the battery. Which set of battery items matches the manual?

answers.text: Check battery age by reading the manufacture date on the label
Check the battery warranty card and verify it is still in force
Check battery fluid level, connections, and tie-downs; battery must not be broken or leaking and must be secured against movement
Check only the battery terminal color coding (red = positive)

explanations.a: Battery age by label is not what the manual's inspection covers.
explanations.b: Warranty cards are not part of the CDL pre-trip battery check.
explanations.c: The CDL manual specifies checking battery fluid level, connections, and tie-downs; the battery must not be broken or leaking and must be secured against movement.
explanations.d: Terminal color alone is not the scope of the manual's battery check.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: During the engine compartment check, the CDL manual requires inspecting the drive belts on certain critical components. Which components does the manual specifically mention, and what must be checked?

answers.text: Check only the serpentine belt for the alternator; other belts are optional
Check all v-belts for proper color only; white belts indicate overheating
Check fan and accessory belts for tension by applying static load per the specification plate
Check belts for tightness and excessive wear on the alternator, water pump, and air compressor; learn how much give each belt should have when adjusted right

explanations.a: The manual covers more than just the alternator belt.
explanations.b: Belt color is not the manual's inspection criterion.
explanations.c: Applying a static load per spec plate is more detailed than the manual's pre-trip procedure.
explanations.d: The CDL manual specifies checking belts for tightness and excessive wear on the alternator, water pump, and air compressor, and instructs the driver to learn how much give each belt should have when adjusted correctly.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: The CDL manual lists windshield washer fluid as a required check during Step 2. Why is this item included in the engine compartment inspection?

answers.text: The washer fluid reservoir is typically located in the engine compartment and is needed to maintain visibility, especially in winter and rain
Washer fluid is also used to top off the power steering system when it runs low
Washer fluid is used to cool the air compressor in hot weather
Federal law requires washer fluid to be replaced at every pre-trip inspection

explanations.a: The CDL manual includes windshield washer fluid in the engine-compartment check because the reservoir is there; maintaining it supports visibility in all conditions.
explanations.b: Washer fluid and power steering fluid are entirely separate systems.
explanations.c: Washer fluid has no cooling function for the air compressor.
explanations.d: There is no federal requirement to replace washer fluid at every pre-trip; the check is simply to verify there is enough.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: After checking fluid levels, the CDL manual requires looking for leaks in the engine compartment. Which set of fluids does the manual list as sources to check for leaks?

answers.text: Only engine oil leaks need to be checked; other fluids are minor
Fuel, coolant, oil, power steering fluid, hydraulic fluid, and battery fluid
Only external leaks visible from outside the cab
Leaks are checked only after the engine warms up fully, not during the pre-trip

explanations.a: The manual's leak-check scope goes well beyond engine oil.
explanations.b: The CDL manual lists the engine-compartment leak check as covering fuel, coolant, oil, power steering fluid, hydraulic fluid, and battery fluid.
explanations.c: Leaks inside the engine compartment — not just visible from outside the cab — are on the manual's list.
explanations.d: The manual requires pre-trip leak checks regardless of engine temperature.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: During Step 2, the CDL manual includes a check on the electrical wiring. What specific wiring defect does the manual tell drivers to look for?

answers.text: Look for wiring that is not the correct color for the circuit
Look for wiring that is not zip-tied every six inches
Look for cracked or worn electrical wiring insulation
Look for wiring that was installed after the original factory build

explanations.a: Wire color coding is a design specification, not the pre-trip defect the manual identifies.
explanations.b: Zip-tie spacing is not the manual's wiring check criterion.
explanations.c: The CDL manual specifies looking for cracked or worn electrical wiring insulation during the engine compartment check.
explanations.d: Post-factory wiring modifications are not the defect the manual's pre-trip targets.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: At the end of Step 2, after completing all engine compartment checks, the CDL manual gives a specific instruction about the hood or cab. Which instruction matches the manual?

answers.text: Leave the hood propped open so the engine runs cooler during the trip
Tape the hood latch with safety tape if any cracks are found
Remove the hood-prop rod and discard it to prevent interference with the fan
Lower and secure the hood, cab, or engine compartment door

explanations.a: Driving with the hood open is unsafe and not the manual's instruction.
explanations.b: Taping a cracked latch is not the manual's procedure; a cracked latch is a defect that must be repaired.
explanations.c: Removing the prop rod is not the manual's instruction.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to lower and secure the hood, cab, or engine compartment door after completing the engine compartment checks.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: For vehicles with an automatic transmission, the CDL manual notes a special condition for checking the transmission fluid. Which condition matches the manual?

answers.text: Automatic transmission fluid level may require the engine to be running when the fluid is checked
ATF is checked only when the vehicle has been sitting for 24 hours
ATF does not need to be checked as part of the pre-trip inspection
ATF is filled automatically by the engine oil system

explanations.a: The CDL manual notes that automatic transmission fluid level may require the engine to be running when checked, unlike most other fluids.
explanations.b: A 24-hour sit requirement is not the manual's condition for ATF check.
explanations.c: ATF is explicitly listed in the manual's Step 2 fluid checklist.
explanations.d: ATF and engine oil are separate systems; ATF is not auto-filled by engine oil.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Before raising the hood to begin Step 2 of the seven-step inspection, the CDL manual states a pre-condition involving the parking brakes. Which pre-condition matches the manual?

answers.text: The parking brake must be released so the vehicle can roll clear of any oil leak
The parking brakes must be on and/or the wheels must be chocked to prevent the vehicle from moving
The parking brake is set only if the vehicle is on a grade greater than 3 percent
The parking brake is set only if the trailer is attached

explanations.a: Releasing the parking brake before entering the engine compartment creates an unsafe rolling hazard.
explanations.b: The CDL manual specifies the parking brakes must be on and/or wheels chocked before opening the hood or engine compartment.
explanations.c: The manual requires the brake to be set before opening the hood regardless of grade.
explanations.d: The pre-condition applies equally to solo tractors and combinations.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Depending on vehicle design, the CDL manual describes different ways to access the engine compartment for Step 2. Which options does the manual mention?

answers.text: The engine is always accessed from underneath with a creeper
The engine access hatch on the roof is the primary entry point
Raising the hood, tilting the cab and securing loose items so they don't fall and break something, or opening the engine compartment door
Engine compartment access requires a licensed mechanic to be present

explanations.a: Underbelly creeper access is a maintenance procedure, not the inspection method.
explanations.b: Roof hatches are not a standard engine compartment access method.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states the driver may have to raise the hood, tilt the cab (securing loose things so they don't fall and break something), or open the engine compartment door for Step 2.
explanations.d: The driver performs Step 2 independently; a mechanic is not required.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.keyword: warning lights go out right away
questions.text: After starting the engine in Step 3, the CDL manual describes how warning lights and buzzers should behave if the vehicle is in good condition. Which behavior matches the manual?

answers.text: Warning lights should stay on permanently to confirm the monitoring system is active
Oil, coolant, and charging circuit warning lights should stay on until the engine reaches operating temperature
Warning lights should blink twice and then go out
Oil, coolant, charging circuit, and antilock brake system warning lights should go out right away after engine start

explanations.a: Warning lights that stay on indicate a fault, not normal operation.
explanations.b: On a properly functioning vehicle, these lights do not stay on until warm-up.
explanations.c: A two-blink pattern is not the manual's described normal behavior.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states that oil, coolant, charging circuit warning, and antilock brake system lights should go out right away after engine start on a vehicle in good condition.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: The CDL manual includes a specific ABS indicator light check during Step 3. What normal behavior should the driver see from the ABS light if the system is working properly?

answers.text: The ABS light should come on briefly and then turn off; if it stays on, the ABS is not working properly
The ABS light should stay on permanently to indicate the system is in standby
The ABS light should flash three times and then stay dark
The ABS light is not checked during the pre-trip inspection

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the ABS indicator light on the dash should come on and then turn off; if it stays on, the ABS is not working properly.
explanations.b: An ABS light that stays on permanently indicates a malfunction, not standby.
explanations.c: A three-flash pattern is not the normal ABS self-test behavior described in the manual.
explanations.d: The ABS light check is explicitly listed in the manual's Step 3 procedure.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: During Step 3 of the seven-step inspection, the CDL manual includes a check of the ammeter or voltmeter on the dashboard. What should those gauges show if the charging system is functioning correctly?

answers.text: They should show a full discharge to confirm alternator load
They should be in the normal range(s)
They should read exactly 13.8 volts or the needle is in the red zone
They should be turned off to avoid battery drain

explanations.a: A full discharge reading would indicate a fault, not normal operation.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to check that the ammeter and/or voltmeter is in the normal range(s) after starting the engine.
explanations.c: The manual does not specify a particular voltage value; it uses the general guidance of normal range.
explanations.d: The ammeter or voltmeter is a read-only gauge; it cannot be turned off.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.keyword: coolant and oil temp gradual rise
questions.text: After starting the engine, the CDL manual describes how the coolant temperature and engine oil temperature gauges should behave. Which behavior matches the manual?

answers.text: Both should immediately jump to operating temperature within 10 seconds
Both should stay completely flat for the first two minutes and then spike
Both should begin a gradual rise toward the normal operating range
Both should start in the red zone and fall to normal as the engine warms up

explanations.a: Immediately jumping to operating temperature in 10 seconds would indicate a thermostat fault.
explanations.b: A flat then spike pattern is not normal engine warm-up behavior.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states both coolant temperature and engine oil temperature should begin a gradual rise to the normal operating range after engine start.
explanations.d: Gauges do not start in the red zone on a properly functioning engine.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: The CDL manual specifies how quickly the oil pressure gauge should respond after the engine is started. Which description matches the manual?

answers.text: Oil pressure should not rise for at least two minutes while the oil warms up
Oil pressure should remain at zero until the engine reaches 1,500 rpm
Oil pressure should take about five minutes to rise to the minimum safe level
Oil pressure should come up to normal within seconds after the engine is started

explanations.a: A two-minute delay in oil pressure would indicate a serious lubrication failure.
explanations.b: Oil pressure must build as soon as the oil pump begins turning, not only at 1,500 rpm.
explanations.c: Five minutes is far too long; that would indicate a dangerously extended period without adequate lubrication.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states oil pressure should come up to normal within seconds after the engine is started.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: During Step 3, the CDL manual gives a comprehensive list of controls the driver must check. Which set of controls matches the manual's list?

answers.text: Steering wheel, clutch, accelerator, foot brake, trailer brake, parking brake, retarder controls, and transmission controls — checking all for looseness, sticking, damage, or improper setting
Only the steering wheel and the horn
Only the turn signals and hazard lights
Only the cruise control and the radio

explanations.a: The CDL manual specifies checking all of the following for looseness, sticking, damage, or improper setting: steering wheel, clutch, accelerator, brake controls (foot, trailer, and parking), retarder controls, and transmission controls.
explanations.b: Only checking the steering wheel and horn is far below the manual's required scope.
explanations.c: Turn signals and hazards are checked in Steps 4 and 6, not the full Step 3 control check.
explanations.d: Cruise control and radio are not among the safety-critical controls the manual lists for Step 3.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: The CDL manual includes a mirrors and windshield check during Step 3. What defects does the manual say to look for?

answers.text: Look only for broken mirror glass; scratches are acceptable
Inspect mirrors and windshield for cracks, dirt, illegal stickers, or other obstructions to seeing clearly; clean and adjust as necessary
Check only that the mirrors are the manufacturer-approved size
Verify the windshield tint meets the legal minimum light-transmission value

explanations.a: Scratches can reduce visibility; the manual's scope includes any obstruction to clear vision.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to inspect mirrors and windshield for cracks, dirt, illegal stickers, or other obstructions to seeing clearly, and to clean and adjust as necessary.
explanations.c: Mirror size is not the pre-trip check item; condition and adjustment are.
explanations.d: Tint measurement is not part of the manual's Step 3 windshield check.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: Step 3 includes a safety belt check. According to the CDL manual, what conditions must the safety belt meet?

answers.text: The safety belt must be a minimum of three inches wide and rated for 10,000 pounds
The safety belt only needs to fasten; wear and fraying are acceptable if the buckle works
The safety belt must be securely mounted, must adjust and latch properly, and must not be ripped or frayed
The safety belt must have a reflective strip on the shoulder portion

explanations.a: Width and tensile rating are manufacturer specifications, not the manual's pre-trip check criteria.
explanations.b: Ripped or frayed belts are explicitly listed as a defect in the manual.
explanations.c: The CDL manual specifies the safety belt must be securely mounted, must adjust and latch properly, and must not be ripped or frayed.
explanations.d: Reflective strips are not part of the manual's safety belt inspection criteria.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.text: The CDL manual gives a specific steering wheel play limit during the defects overview. At what amount of play does the manual say steering becomes hard?

answers.text: More than 2 degrees of play, or about 1/4 inch at the rim of a 20-inch wheel
More than 5 degrees of play, or about 1 inch at the rim of a 20-inch wheel
More than 15 degrees of play, or about 3 inches at the rim of a 20-inch wheel
More than 10 degrees of play, approximately 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch steering wheel

explanations.a: 2 degrees and 1/4 inch are below the manual's stated limit.
explanations.b: 5 degrees and 1 inch are below the manual's stated limit.
explanations.c: 15 degrees and 3 inches exceed the manual's stated limit.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees (approximately 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch steering wheel) can make it hard to steer.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.text: During the walk-around, the CDL manual specifies minimum tire tread depths. What are the minimums for front tires and for all other tires?

answers.text: At least 4/32 inch in every major groove on front tires, and at least 2/32 inch on other tires
At least 2/32 inch on all tires including front tires
At least 8/32 inch on front tires and 4/32 inch on other tires
Tread depth is not checked during the pre-trip; only visual bulge inspection is required

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the minimum tread depth is 4/32 inch in every major groove on front tires and at least 2/32 inch on other tires.
explanations.b: 2/32 inch applies to non-front tires, not front tires, which have a stricter standard.
explanations.c: 8/32 and 4/32 exceed the manual's stated minimums; those are higher standards than required.
explanations.d: Tread depth is explicitly listed as a required check during the walk-around.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.text: During Step 4, the CDL manual gives a specific reason for taking the key with you when you exit the cab. Which reason matches the manual?

answers.text: So the key is available immediately if the engine needs to be restarted during the walk-around
So someone else won't move the truck while the driver is outside inspecting it
Because federal regulations prohibit leaving the key in the ignition when the engine is off
So the key can be used to scratch rust off the lug nuts for inspection

explanations.a: The engine is off during the walk-around; restarting it mid-walk-around is not the reason.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the driver should take the key because in a later step when checking under the fifth wheel or the trailer, the driver does not want someone else to move the truck and injure them.
explanations.c: There is no federal prohibition on keys-in-ignition with engine off in this context in the manual.
explanations.d: Using the key to scratch lug nuts is not the purpose described in the manual.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.keyword: parking brake then service brake test
questions.text: In Step 7 of the seven-step inspection, the CDL manual prescribes a two-part brake system test in a specific sequence. Which sequence matches the manual?

answers.text: Service brake test first at highway speed, then parking brake test on a grade
Both tests simultaneously while the vehicle is stationary
Parking brake test first (pull gently forward in a low gear against the set parking brake), then service brake test (move forward at about 5 mph and apply firmly)
Only the parking brake test; service brake testing is optional on pre-trip

explanations.a: The order in the manual is parking before service, and service brakes are not tested at highway speed.
explanations.b: The service brake test requires forward motion; both cannot be done simultaneously while stationary.
explanations.c: The CDL manual prescribes testing the parking brake first by gently pulling forward in a low gear against the set brake, then testing service brakes by moving forward at about 5 mph and applying the pedal firmly.
explanations.d: Service brake testing is explicitly required in the manual's Step 7.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.text: During the walk-around suspension check, the CDL manual identifies a specific leaf-spring threshold that puts the vehicle out of service. Which threshold matches the manual?

answers.text: If any single leaf is cracked, the vehicle is immediately out of service
If half the leaves are missing, the vehicle may still be operated at reduced speed
If one leaf is bent, the vehicle is out of service
If one-fourth or more of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, it will put the vehicle out of service — though any defect could be dangerous

explanations.a: A single cracked leaf is a defect the manual notes as dangerous, but the specific out-of-service threshold is one-fourth missing.
explanations.b: Operating at reduced speed with half the leaves missing is not the manual's guidance.
explanations.c: A bent leaf is a defect but one bent leaf alone is not the manual's defined out-of-service threshold.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states that if one-fourth or more of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, it will put the vehicle out of service, though any defect could be dangerous.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.text: The CDL manual requires three types of emergency equipment on CMVs. Which set of three matches the manual?

answers.text: Fire extinguisher (properly charged and rated), spare electrical fuses (unless equipped with circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles (such as three reflective triangles, 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares)
First aid kit, fire extinguisher, and a spare tire
Road flares only, at least ten per vehicle
Flashing amber beacon, emergency triangles, and a spare wheel

explanations.a: The CDL manual specifies the three required items as a properly charged and rated fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles such as three reflective triangles, 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares.
explanations.b: A first aid kit is optional, not required, and a spare tire is not listed as required emergency equipment.
explanations.c: The manual allows alternative warning devices; it does not require ten flares.
explanations.d: An amber beacon is not in the manual's three-item required list.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.text: During the walk-around, the CDL manual requires checking the wheel hub area for a specific fluid condition. Which condition matches the manual?

answers.text: Hub oil levels must be topped off daily during the pre-trip
Hub oil level should be checked and seals must not be leaking
Hub areas are exempt from pre-trip inspection under FMCSA rules
Hub caps must show the date of the last gear-oil replacement

explanations.a: Hub oil is topped off during maintenance, not the pre-trip; the pre-trip check is for level and leakage.
explanations.b: The CDL manual specifies checking hub oil level and ensuring hub oil seals are not leaking during the wheel-and-hub walk-around check.
explanations.c: Hub areas are explicitly included in the walk-around; they are not exempt.
explanations.d: Maintenance date labels on hub caps are not the manual's required check.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.keyword: exhaust system not touching wires fuel lines
questions.text: During the walk-around, the CDL manual specifies what exhaust system defects to look for. Which set of defects matches the manual?

answers.text: Loose, broken, or missing exhaust pipes, mufflers, and tailpipes; and exhaust system parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other moving parts
Only rust on exhaust pipes; no other exhaust defects are listed
Loose, broken, or missing exhaust pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, or stacks; loose or missing mounting hardware; and exhaust parts leaking, rubbing against fuel, tires, air-lines, or wires
Only exhaust leaks detectable by smell inside the cab are listed as defects

explanations.a: This list is close but the manual also includes stacks, mounting brackets, and the proximity to air-lines and wiring.
explanations.b: The manual's exhaust defect list is broader than rust alone.
explanations.c: The CDL manual lists loose, broken, or missing exhaust pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, or vertical stacks; loose, broken, or missing mounting brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts; and exhaust system parts rubbing against fuel, tires, or other moving parts, and parts that are leaking.
explanations.d: Cab smell alone is not the complete defect list; physical inspection of the system is required.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.keyword: rust streaked lug nuts wrench check
questions.text: During the walk-around, the CDL manual identifies a specific sign that lug nuts may be loose and describes how to verify them. Which sign and method match the manual?

answers.text: Lug nuts painted yellow indicate they were recently overtorqued; use a hammer to check
Shiny lug nuts indicate recent removal; count them and compare with the spec plate
Any lug nut with visible paint indicates a recall; contact the manufacturer
Rust streaks around lug nuts may mean the nuts are loose; use a wrench to test their tightness

explanations.a: Yellow paint on lug nuts is not the manual's defect indicator.
explanations.b: Shiny lug nuts are not the manual's defect indicator.
explanations.c: Paint on lug nuts is not a recall indicator in the manual.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states that rust streaks around wheel nuts may mean the nuts are loose, and instructs drivers to use a wrench to test their tightness.

questions.name: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection
questions.objective: 6.5 Air brake check (the 7-step air brake test merged with general inspection)
questions.text: When testing the service brakes during Step 7, the CDL manual says the driver should watch for two specific problems. Which pair matches the manual?

answers.text: Pulling to one side or the other, and unusual brake pedal feel or delayed stopping action
Excessive engine braking and automatic gear downshifting
Wheel lockup and automatic ABS activation at 5 mph
Air pressure drop below 60 psi and brake light flicker

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the driver should watch for pulling to one side or the other, and any unusual brake pedal feel or delayed stopping action during the Step 7 service brake test.
explanations.b: Engine braking and downshifting are not the defects the service brake test is designed to catch.
explanations.c: ABS activation is normal at threshold braking; it is not a Step 7 defect indicator.
explanations.d: Air pressure drop and brake light flicker are not the manual's listed Step 7 service brake indicators.
